questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.explanation: Article 38 deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: What is the name of the committee that was constituted in West Bengal to review the state's police force and suggest reforms?
questions.explanation: The Gurupada Chakraborty Committee was constituted in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is not available to a foreigner in India?
questions.explanation: The Right to Freedom of Residence is not available to a foreigner in India.

questions.question: What is the name of the amendment to the Indian Constitution that introduced the concept of reservation for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: The Seventy-First Amendment Act introduced the concept of reservation for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal has a three-tier system of Panchayats.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a major distributary of the Ganges River in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Damodar River originates in the Chhotanagpur Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges is situated in the northern part of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Bhutan Himalayas extend into northern West Bengal.

questions.question: Which delta is the largest in India, and is located in the southern part of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is also known as the Sundarbans Delta.

questions.question: Which of the following districts is the largest in West Bengal by area?
questions.explanation: Alipurduar District is the largest in West Bengal by area.

questions.question: Which of the following states shares the least international border with West Bengal?
questions.explanation: West Bengal shares the least international border with Bihar.

questions.question: Which Indian city hosted the Miss United Nations 2025 pageant, and its winner is from West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The winner of Miss United Nations 2025 pageant is from West Bengal.

questions.question: Which river in West Bengal is known for its Sundarbans Delta?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans Delta is formed by the Ganges River in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which festival was celebrated in the state of West Bengal in 2025?
questions.explanation: Lokkhi Puja is a significant festival in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which scheme is initiated by the West Bengal government to provide financial assistance to farmers?
questions.explanation: Mukhyamantri Krishi Saathi Yojana is initiated by the West Bengal government.

questions.question: Which international organisation has signed an MoU with the West Bengal government to develop the state's IT sector?
questions.explanation: NASSCOM has signed an MoU with the West Bengal government.

questions.question: If the Simple Interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at 12% per annum is Rs. 540, the Compound Interest for 2 years at the same rate will be?
questions.explanation: Compound Interest is the difference between the amount and principal in the second year.

questions.question: A sum of money placed at compound interest at the rate of 10% per annum for 2 years amounts to Rs. 121.10. The sum of money is?
questions.explanation: The sum of money can be found using the compound interest formula.

questions.question: What is the rate of interest p.a. at which a sum of money will become four times itself in 2 years?
questions.explanation: The rate of interest can be found using the compound interest formula.

questions.question: If Rs. 1000 amounts to Rs. 1331 in 2 years at compound interest, the rate of interest is?
questions.explanation: The rate of interest can be found using the compound interest formula.

questions.question: A certain amount of money at compound interest compounded annually becomes Rs. 4000 in 2 years. The amount becomes Rs. 9000 in?
questions.explanation: The amount can be found using the compound interest formula.

questions.question: A contractor has to complete a railway bridge in 120 days. He employs 120 men on the project. After 60 days, he realises that the work is only half complete. How many more days will it take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: The work is half complete, so it will take twice the time to complete the entire work.

questions.question: A pipe can fill 1/4th of a tank in 2 hours. How long will it take to fill the entire tank?
questions.explanation: The pipe can fill 1/4th of the tank in 2 hours, so it will take 4 times to fill the entire tank.

questions.question: A group of workers can complete a piece of work in 12 days. If 2/5th of the work is completed by 1/3rd of the workers, how much work will be left to do?
questions.explanation: If 2/5th of the work is completed, 3/5th of the work is left.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 25 hours respectively. How long will it take to fill the tank with both pipes working together?
questions.explanation: The combined rate of two pipes is the sum of the rates of two pipes.

questions.question: A train travels from Sealdah to Howrah at an average speed of 40 km/h. If the distance between the two stations is 20 km, how many hours will it take to cover the distance?
questions.explanation: Speed multiplied by time equals distance.

questions.question: A man walking at a speed of 4 km/hr covers a certain distance in 8 hours. How much time, in hours, will he take to cover twice the distance at the same speed?
questions.explanation: Time taken is inversely proportional to distance.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 240 km in 3 hours. What is the speed of the car in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time.

questions.question: A train travels from Sealdah to Howrah covering a distance of 24 km in 2 minutes. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, and time should be in hours.

questions.question: A man travels from Kolkata to Digha at an average speed of 60 km/hr and returns to Kolkata at an average speed of 40 km/hr. What is his average speed for the entire trip?
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

questions.question: A bus travels from New Town to Rajarhat at an average speed of 25 km/hr and covers a distance of 75 km. What is the time taken by the bus to cover this distance?
questions.explanation: Time taken is distance divided by speed.

questions.question: A code is given as: H 13, L 6, E 5, O 15, M 3. Which word is encoded?
questions.explanation: The code represents the last digit of the alphabetical order of the letters.

questions.question: In a particular code: 1=|, 2=*, 3=+, 4=/. What is the code for the word ‘POND’?
questions.explanation: The code represents the word by replacing each letter with the corresponding symbol.

questions.question: A code is given: 1=A, 2=B, 3=C, 4=D. If ‘ABC’ is encoded as ‘123’, then what is the code for ‘BCD’?
questions.explanation: The code represents the word by replacing each letter with the corresponding digit in alphabetical order.

questions.question: In a particular code: A=1, B=2, C=3. What is the code for the word ‘CAB’?
questions.explanation: The code represents the word by replacing each letter with the corresponding digit.

questions.question: A code is given: 1=+, 2=*, 3=-. If ‘12’ is encoded as ‘+-’, then what is the code for ‘24’?
questions.explanation: The code represents the digits by replacing with the corresponding operators.

questions.question: From the Howrah Bridge, if you walk 500 meters towards the Hooghly River, then turn right and walk for 300 meters, then turn left and walk for 200 meters, which direction are you facing?
questions.explanation: You turn left after walking towards the Hooghly River.

questions.question: You are standing at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple and you walk 150 meters towards the Ganges River, then turn right and walk for 200 meters, then turn left and walk for 250 meters. Which temple are you facing?
questions.explanation: You turn left after walking towards the Ganges River.

questions.question: A person starts walking from the Esplanade Metro Station, walks 400 meters towards the north, then turns left and walks 200 meters, then turns left again and walks 300 meters. Which direction is the person facing now?
questions.explanation: He turns left after walking towards the north.

questions.question: A man is standing at the Victoria Memorial facing the west. If he walks 100 meters, turns right and walks 200 meters, then turns right and walks 150 meters, in which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: He turns right after walking towards the west.

questions.question: A woman walks 500 meters from the Park Circus Crossing towards the north, then turns left and walks 300 meters. Then, she turns right and walks 200 meters and finally turns left and walks 150 meters. Which direction is the woman facing at the end?
questions.explanation: She turns left after walking towards the north.

questions.question: In a sequence where the first term is 3, and each successive term is obtained by adding 2, 3, 4, and so on, what will be the 10th term in the series?
questions.explanation: Each term in the series increases by consecutive integers.

questions.question: The sequence starts with the digits 4, 9, 16, 25. If the pattern continues, what will be the next term in the series?
questions.explanation: The pattern is formed by squaring consecutive integers.

questions.question: The sequence starts with the letters A, D, G, J. If the pattern continues, what will be the next letter in the series?
questions.explanation: The pattern is formed by adding 3 consecutive letters.

questions.question: In a series where the first term is 2, and each successive term is obtained by multiplying by 2, what will be the 5th term in the series?
questions.explanation: Each term in the series is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 2.

questions.question: The sequence starts with the numbers 1, 2, 4, 7. If the pattern continues, what will be the next number in the series?
questions.explanation: The pattern is formed by adding consecutive integers.
